blind_target.title: Wine for the Table: Self-Construal, Group Size, and Choice for Self and Others
blind_target.evidence_quote: The JCR paper contains six studies, all of which were conducted on MTurk. We chose to try to replicate Study 3 because it seemed to have the best statistical evidence, as it was supported by the smallest p-value in the paper: t(239) = 2.20, p = .03
blind_target.outcome_quote: Let us first consider whether the original result was significant in the more highly powered replication attempts. In this case, the results are mixed. In the first replication attempt (with the typo), the three-way interaction among prime, group size, and preference for nonfiction was significant and in the same direction as in the original study: b = .162, SE = .070, p = .022. But in the second replication attempt (with no typo), that same interaction did not approach significance, though it was still in the same direction: b = .050, SE = .064, p = .432
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly call the two attempts mixed and describe significant agreement in the first and failure in the second; their summary also notes inconsistency with the hypothesized pattern. The original authors’ feedback is not the replicators’ verdict.
